title: La misa
goal: Talk about mass without pretending to be devout
culture: She will ask, and lying is worse than saying no. The honest answer given respectfully is completely acceptable here — what is not acceptable is being dismissive about it. Primero Dios is said by believers and non-believers alike; it means we will see.

beats.es: ¿Y usted no viene a misa, joven? No lo he visto.
beats.objective: Say you are not from here
beats.good: It is the true answer and it is not a brush-off. Doña on the end is what makes it courteous rather than defensive.

beats.es: Ah, pero Dios está en todas partes, mi hijo.
beats.en: I have a lot of respect for it.
beats.good: Respect without agreement, said plainly. She will accept it, because it is the answer she was actually asking for.

beats.es: Bueno. Ahí lo espero un domingo.
beats.good: Algún día is a soft maybe that neither of you will hold the other to. Saying never would be answering a question she did not ask.

beats.es: Primero Dios, mi hijo. Primero Dios.
beats.objective: Answer it the way it is meant
beats.good: Primero Dios is said by everybody here, devout or not. It means we will see, and answering it back closes the conversation warmly and commits you to nothing.
